chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Nafi', from Abi Khalid al-Qammat, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to flog the Jew and the Christian, concerning wine and intoxicating nabidh, with eighty lashes when they drank it openly in a city among the cities; but if they drank it in their churches and synagogues, he would not interfere with them unless they came to be among the Muslims.

key_terms.أَظْهَرُوا شُرْبَهُ: they made their drinking public or open
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, identified here as the authority implementing the ruling
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine, the intoxicant explicitly mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: among the Muslims, meaning within the public Muslim social space
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً: eighty lashes, the prescribed corporal punishment mentioned in the report
key_terms.كَنَائِسِهِمْ: their churches, referring to Christian places of worship
key_terms.مُسْكِرِ النَّبِيذِ: intoxicating nabidh, a fermented drink that causes intoxication

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in this hadith on Jews and Christians drinking wine openly in a Muslim city?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal practice of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding non-Muslims who openly consumed intoxicants in Muslim public spaces. It distinguishes between public manifestation in the Muslim polity, where the hadd was enforced, and private practice within their own religious spaces, where no interference occurred unless it entered the public sphere of Muslims.
